title: Everton’s David Moyes calls for Premier League clarity over Chelsea sanctions
content:
Everton manager David Moyes has called for clarity over why Chelsea escaped a points deduction for their historical breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules.

Chelsea were given a one-year ban, suspended for two years, from signing first-team players and handed a £10million ($13.7m; €11.6m) fine on March 16 following charges relating to incomplete financial reporting and missed payments during Roman Abramovich’s time as owner.

The charges are from 10 years ago and would not have impacted the club’s compliance with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules (PSR).

Everton were given two points deductions totalling eight points during the 2023-24 campaign for PSR breaches. Moyes has called for greater explanation in the difference in punishment ahead of Everton hosting Chelsea on Sunday.

“I don’t think they have explained it well enough in the reasoning what the fine was and why it was,” Moyes told a press conference on Friday, in quotes carried by the Guardian. “I think they have to explain exactly what has happened here. If they don’t then we are never going to understand their reasoning why.

“This is me not being anything against Chelsea, absolutely not, I’m just saying that everybody would like to know; Everton supporters, for the pain they had to go through when they had a huge points deduction, and other clubs as well. Those points deductions may well have been correct, I don’t know, but we need to see what is the difference?

“What would you rather have, a £10m fine or a 10 point deduction? The money you get for your league place now, that might cover it. It would be good if we could get more of an explanation. How much is the £10m fine having an effect, really?”

A sanction agreement published by the Premier League outlined that between 2011 and 2018, Chelsea paid more than £23m to seven unregistered agents “or entities associated with them” in connection with the transfer and registration of seven players. A total of £47,524,925.74 was paid to 12 individuals or corporate entities, “each of which implicated one or more of the rules” during that time.

The sanction agreement stated the fine and transfer ban would have been more significant had BlueCo not self-reported the breaches after purchasing the club from Abramovich in 2022.

Everton were deducted 10 points, later reduced to six, in November 2023 for exceeding the PSR threshold by £19.5m for the three-year reporting period ending in 2021-22. They were handed a two-point penalty for a breach of £16.6m for the reporting period ending in 2022-23.

Nottingham Forest were also penalised during the 2023-24 season and were handed a four-point penalty for exceeding the PSR threshold by £34.5m for the cycle ending in 2022-23.
